scope: Standalone staged ABI-v2 IPv4 NAT with incarnation-keyed TCP generations, lifecycle and options. Not installed by the agent.

maps.tcp: gr8s_nat_tcp_v2: hash key32/value64, max65536, no preallocation. Key originaltuple16 + source incarnation16. Value reuses proven v1 sequence/window/timestamp state ABI.

kernel.environment: Disposable Fedora 44 VM22291, kernel6.19.10-300.fc44.x86_64. BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN, FD-only maps/programs. All five programs verified; owned run directory removed.
kernel.difference: Two nonlinear-skb cases are interpreter-only. Kernel tests otherwise run the same functions.

regression.networkingScope: Networking suite after initial TCP port; subsequent source change only reuses NAT compiler scratch, covered by final bytecode/kernel tests.
regression.v1Scope: Existing v1 fixture, existing expected drop behavior remains the default in the shared TCP suite.

behavior: Preflight a pure SYN under both tuple reservations before selecting a new backend. Safe generation replacement reuses existing ISN/timestamp evidence and removes only its paired return claim and TCP state.
TCP state is observed at commit/restore after caller policy approval. Active/time writes use a forward map pointer while both reservations are held.
Pending NAT claims remain inactive when TCP metadata publication fails; replies cannot use them. Existing metadata owner remains intact.
SYN-only lifetime120s, established2h, closed120s, reset10s. Invalid/stale controls do not refresh tombstones. Pending policy claim lifetime remains5s and UDP180s.
Existing sequence, ACK/window, timestamps, option parsing, simultaneous open, early-data handshake/refusal and reordered closure checks run through staged v2.

Four interleaved TCP streams share one client port: two VIPs, direct backend and self-backend hairpin. They retain independent ISN/timestamp state; replacing one alias-backed stream preserves the other three.
retiredReplySemantics: Once an old return claim is removed, traffic to an ordinary primary address passes unchanged without touching the new TCP state. The adapter explicitly checks absent ownership and unchanged packet/state. Unclaimed private-alias replies fail closed. A stale SYN-ACK through the current claimed tuple is rejected by TCP generation checks. No claim is made that arbitrary unmatched primary traffic is universally dropped.
developmentCorrections: Initial compiler exceeded stack limit at520bytes (260struct/248spill/12key). Reusing32-byte epoch-key/return scratch and forward map pointers made all five programs compile and verify. Compiler output did not identify the failing stage.

The existing TCP fixture originally expected a drop for a removed old return claim. The staged adapter now requests and verifies unchanged pass-through only for this unclaimed primary-address case; v1 default expectations remain unchanged.
The root harness initially rejected a Python bytearray in ctypes before running the malformed-packet case. Converting input to bytes fixed the harness; final kernel suite passed.
limits: Synthetic packets, not live TCP sockets or actual CNI/native/Kata translation.
Policy approval is modeled by stage selection; actual alias-aware NetworkPolicy enforcement and peer-generation reply state remain outstanding.
Identity/readiness rows are supplied by the fixture; distributed receiving-node installation acknowledgment remains outstanding.
No bounded v2 GC/scanner or retained-flow migration/upgrade integration yet. Capacity recovery in the packet fixture manually frees map entries.
Agent attachment, live guest/native TCP/UDP hairpin/collision/restart proof, IPv6 packet NAT, packet NodePort and broader parent Service semantics remain required.
remaining: Parent podster-p9c and child podster-p9c.10 remain in progress.
